basic_identification.full_title: Specification for Capacitors for Electric Fan Motors (First Revision) (बिजली के पंखे के मोटरों के लिए संधारित्रों (कैपेसिटरों) की विशिष्टि (पहला पुनरीक्षण))
basic_identification.sector_category: Electrotechnical / Power Capacitors (approved by the Electrotechnical Division Council and finalized by the Power Capacitors Sectional Committee, ETD 29, formerly under ETDC 29/ETD 03, of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

scope.summary: This Indian Standard prescribes the manufacturing requirements, design configurations, electrical ratings, safety features, and performance testing protocols for motor run capacitors (typically dry type, self-healing, metallized polypropylene film - MPP) used with single-phase induction motors of electric fans (including ceiling, table, pedestal, and cabin fans) conforming to IS 374, IS 555, and IS 1169.

certification_and_marking.standard_type: Material Product Specification (Electrotechnical Department / Power Capacitors, ETD 29)
certification_and_marking.certification_status: Voluntary Product Specification. However, under the mandatory quality control orders (QCO) for electric ceiling, table, and pedestal fans, the auxiliary motor capacitors are legally required to carry the prestigious physical ISI 'Standard Mark' stamped or embossed on their containers to certify safety and quality compliance.

requirements.detail: Observed or calculated final test values, capacitance percentages, and test voltages must be mathematically rounded off in accordance with IS 2:1960. The decimal places retained should match that of the specified value in the standard.

Capacitor elements are built using high-purity, double-sided aluminum-zinc metallized polypropylene film inside a dry plastic or aluminum container, which is manufactured under dust-controlled, air-conditioned conditions to prevent particulate tracking.

When a localized dielectric breakdown occurs at a weak point in the film, the metallized layer evaporates within 5 to 10 microseconds, extinguishing the arc and instantly restoring the insulation level to its full value.
Standardizes preferred microfarad ratings (1.0 to 10.0 μF), including common domestic sizes: 2.00, 2.25, 2.50, 3.15, and 4.00 μF with standard tolerances restricted to ± 5%.
Designed to operate continuously without thermal runaway or accelerated capacitance droppage across a temperature range of -25°C to +85°C.
The tangent of the loss angle (tan δ) or power factor of the capacitor must not exceed 0.002 (or 0.2%) at rated frequency to prevent localized internal heat generation.
Insulation resistance evaluated under 500 V DC between the terminals and the outer metal container must exceed specified minimum thresholds (typically 3000 seconds) to guarantee user safety.
Under active Amendment No. 3 (June 2020), Clause 7.3.2 (Insulation Resistance between terminals) is completely deleted to streamline dielectric testing and avoid redundant metrics.
Completed capacitors must withstand a sinusoidal AC test potential of 1.5 times the rated voltage between terminals for 10 seconds without dielectric puncture.
To ensure absolute user protection from electric shock, capacitors must withstand 2000 V AC applied between the shorted terminals and the container for 10 seconds without breakdown.
Capacitors must survive continuous heating at +85°C under an overvoltage of 1.25 times the rated voltage for a minimum of 500 hours, with a maximum capacitance droppage of less than 3% to 5%.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 1709 : 1984 (First Revision) is the primary national Indian Standard specification prescribing design, materials, construction, and safety-testing requirements for capacitors used in electric fan motors. Maintained under the Power Capacitors Sectional Committee (ETD 29) and reaffirmed in 2021, the code unifies the manufacturing of ceiling, table, and pedestal fan capacitors. It mandates high-grade metallized polypropylene (MPP) films with self-healing properties that extinguish localized dielectric breakdowns within microseconds, protecting fans from starting failures and electrical short circuits. Incorporating Amendment No. 3 (June 2020), the standard deletes obsolete insulation tests between terminals. To align with modern global standards, IS 1709 is scheduled for formal withdrawal on July 18, 2025, and is transitioning to the consolidated national motor capacitor code IS 2993 (Part 1) : 2024 to support energy-efficient and safe domestic grids.
